profile.subseg: Government IT; PSU Networking; Enterprise Services; O&M
profile.themes: Supply Chain Normalization; Make in India Shift; BFSI Expansion; DPDP Act Compliance

bull_bear.body: Priority given to debt reduction (40% cut) and trade payable clearance (Rs. 30.2 Cr to Rs. 3.77 Cr) to strengthen balance sheet before pursuing growth.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Persistence of global supply chain turbulence beyond 3-4 months; High dependency on government payment cycles; Execution risk in scaling enterprise/BFSI verticals.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Prudent, transparent, and disciplined. Emphasized 'financial discipline' over 'chasing revenue' during crisis. Confident on FY27 recovery based on visible pipeline.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Management deliberately canceled/deferred contracts rather than execute at a loss, a rare move that preserved liquidity while peers (e.g., Allied Digital) reported losses. A Rs. 5 Cr order was voluntarily returned to re-bid under better terms.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Govt/PSU mix currently 85% (60% State, 40% PSUs), targeting shift to 30% State / 40% PSU / 30% Enterprise over 2-3 years to improve cash cycles. New focus on BFSI sector in Mumbai and North East.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Global supply chain normalization and shift to domestic sourcing | Tejas Networks | beneficiary | Med | As a domestic manufacturer, Tejas may gain share if integrators like Takyon aggressively pivot to 'Make in India' hardware to avoid import lead times. |
| Increased demand for data privacy compliance infrastructure | Tata Elxsi | beneficiary | Low | DPDP Act driving inquiries could benefit specialized compliance consultants, though Takyon aims to capture the integration layer itself. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

latest_quarter.body: H2 margins compressed to 5.32% due to component inflation (30-300%) and supply delays (6 weeks to 12 months). New contracts include price escalation clauses; existing book protected via pre-booked OEM pricing.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: 15-20% YoY (surpassing FY25 levels); Margin: 11-13% EBITDA for FY27; Order Inflow: Pipeline growing 15-20% over current book; Capex: Minimal, focus on working capital and vendor pre-payments.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Rs. 32 Cr confirmed (Rs. 12 Cr services/O&M, Rs. 20 Cr supply & installation). Rs. 20-22 Cr expected to bill in H1FY27. Prices for fixed-price portion locked with OEMs.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: DPDP Act compliance projects creating new inquiry pipeline; Geographic expansion into Mumbai (BFSI) and Seven Sister States; Shift to 'Make in India' procurement to bypass global supply shocks.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Takyon Networks prioritized balance sheet repair over toxic revenue in H2FY26, slashing liabilities by 75% while deferring unviable fixed-price projects amid global component inflation. With a protected Rs. 32 Cr order book and supply chains normalizing in 3-4 months, FY27 targets a 15-20% revenue rebound to pre-crisis levels with restored 11-13% EBITDA margins.
